summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, beginning its journey to L2 on a cosmic mapping mission to explore the dark universe. Former President Donald Trump called into the launch press conference to celebrate the liftoff of the observatory—named after the astronomer known as the "Mother of Hubble"—a mission his administration had previously proposed cancelling. In civil space infrastructure, NASA officially brought Deep Space Station 23 online at its Goldstone complex, adding a new 34-meter antenna to the Deep Space Network following a ribbon-cutting event. In scientific research, engineers tested a magnet-powered braking method designed to enable safer, more reusable spacecraft reentries, while laboratory scientists melted a diamond to unlock new insights into the interior mechanisms of ice giant planets. Looking ahead, space watchers should monitor SpaceX as the company prepares for its critical Flight 14 test following a successful static test-fire of its Starship Super Heavy booster.
